There is a deliberate distinction: It answers: How is the digital credential protected?
It answers: Which physical/digital media and verification methods can represent the ticket, and how are QR,
barcode, RFID, NFC, wallet, external credentials and media swapping configured?
That separation is important because the source matrix requires Access Control to transparently support
multiple media technologies while also imposing much deeper security requirements specifically on
Media, Credential & Verification Methods: Board 4 manages the credential/media abstraction layer used by Access Control.
The goal is that an access rule should not care whether the guest presents a QR code, barcode, RFID
wristband, NFC credential, mobile wallet pass, smartphone, hotel room card, biometric identity, or
partner-issued ticket. The system resolves the presented medium to the same virtual ticket/credential and
then sends it to the Access Rules Engine from Board 2.

There are four principles I would explicitly include in the SoftLab SOW.
1. One central Order Engine. POS, B2C, B2B, OTA, Kiosk and Call Center must not
maintain independent order logic. They are channels consuming the same order services.
2. Preserve the commercial snapshot. Once an order is confirmed, TICVAI must preserve
the exact price, discount, tax, fee, dynamic-pricing result and relevant rule/version that
produced the transaction. Later configuration changes must not rewrite historical orders.
3. Reservation and inventory must be transactional. TICVAI cannot create an order
while capacity fails separately and leave the system inconsistent. Capacity locking, payment
state, order confirmation and recovery need proper transaction orchestration.
4. Area 12 is the transaction orchestrator—not a duplicate of other modules.
Pricing stays in Area 10; upgrades/conversions stay in Area 11; ticket media stays in its
credential module; CRM owns the customer master; payment services execute payments;
capacity/inventory engines own availability. Area 12 coordinates all of them into one
governed commercial transaction.
